channel.title: Q7 Quantum Vision Insights
channel.description: Technical notes on cryptographic discovery, migration and quantum engineering.

item.title: What Is a Cryptographic Inventory and Why Does PQC Migration Start There?
item.description: A cryptographic inventory records where cryptography is used, what it protects and how those uses depend on systems and services. It gives a post-quantum migration program an evidence-based starting point.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: CBOM vs Cryptographic Inventory
item.description: A CBOM describes cryptographic components and their properties. A cryptographic inventory places those observations in the context of applications, owners, dependencies and migration decisions.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: A Practical PQC Migration Lifecycle
item.description: Post-quantum migration is a sequence of discovery, inventory, assessment, prioritization, planning and validation activities, revisited as teams learn more about their systems.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: What Crypto-Agility Really Means
item.description: Crypto-agility is the ability to change cryptographic mechanisms with understood impacts. It depends on architecture, governance, testing and operational readiness, not only replaceable code.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: Why PQC Migration Is More Than Replacing RSA and ECC
item.description: A post-quantum transition affects protocols, certificates, devices, dependencies, interoperability and operations. Algorithm selection is one part of a wider engineering program.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: How Simulation Can Reduce PQC Migration Risk
item.description: A controlled simulation can help teams compare migration assumptions, dependencies and operational scenarios before changing production systems. Its value depends on how closely the model represents the real environment.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision

item.title: Quantum Error Correction: From Code Parameters to Hardware Constraints
item.description: Quantum error-correction concepts connect encoding and syndrome information to physical operations, noise models and hardware constraints. Comparing codes requires clearly stated assumptions and metrics.
item.author: Q7 Quantum Vision
